artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a finite set of points, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a collection of $n^2$ lines in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with the following two properties:

(i) no $n$ of the lines in $\mathcal{L}$ lie in a common plane;
(ii) every line $\ell \in \mathcal{L}$ contains at least $n$ points of $A$.

Determine the best possible lower bound on $|A|$ as a function of $n$. In particular, is it true that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $n_0(\varepsilon)$ such that whenever $n \ge n_0(\varepsilon)$ and a configuration $(A, \mathcal{L})$ as above exists, one has
$$|A| \;\gtrsim\; n^{3-\varepsilon} \, ?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (posed by Bourgain) was resolved. Elekes, Kaplan and Sharir (2009/2011), and independently via the polynomial method of Guth and Katz, established the conjectured near-cubic lower bound: under the stated hypotheses |A| = Ω(n^3), confirming Bourgain's conjecture on incidences between points and lines in 3-space. An earlier partial result by Solymosi and Tóth gave the lower bound Ω(n^{11/4}).

status_evidence.title: On lines, joints, and incidences in three dimensions (Elekes, Kaplan, Sharir)
status_evidence.snippet: We give a proof of Bourgain's conjecture on incidences between points and lines in 3-space.
status_evidence.claim: The Bourgain conjecture (the n^{3-ε}, in fact n^3, lower bound for the stated configuration in R^3) was proved.

status_evidence.title: On a question of Bourgain about geometric incidences
status_evidence.snippet: Given s points and n^2 lines in R^3 such that each line is incident to n points but no n lines are coplanar, s = Ω(n^{11/4}).
status_evidence.claim: A partial lower bound Ω(n^{11/4}) was first established, later improved to the full conjectured bound.
